ranking_rationale: Neither bank contains a single revenue-growth number, so the separator was whether a trace noticed that and let its confidence follow: the top traces named the missing prior-quarter and target-quarter growth rates and stayed near 0.5-0.55, while the middle and bottom traces conceded the figure was absent and then poured 0.75-0.90 of the mass onto 'yes' on the strength of an invented central estimate. Bottom place went to factor_memory, whose reasoning argues explicitly for 'no' while the emitted prediction is 'yes', so the central alignment test fails outright.
shared_evidence_note: The banks differ but both are title-only with no revenue figures, so the yes/no split is driven by reasoning discipline rather than evidence content — though E1's extra ad-market and AI-capex headlines gave the two E1 methods concrete headwinds to lean on that the E0 methods never had.
